title: Puducherry Tourism, Hotels & Restaurants: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Puducherry hotel or restaurant sells room-nights and covers, and cash arrives daily at the counter.** Inputs are staff, power, water, food and beverage purchase, OTA commission and rent or EMI; the asset is the building and its fit-out. **Value sits in location and repeat occupancy, not in the kitchen or the linen.** Pricing power is thin in the budget segment and real only where the property is on or near the Beach Promenade or the heritage quarter. **The working-capital cycle is short and favourable: guests pay at checkout, while supplier credit and staff costs run 30 days.** Capex is the risk, not receivables.

## What has changed now
**The one hard local fact is a plan, not traffic: flights to Rajahmundry, Tirupati, Kochi and Kannur are being planned under the revised UDAN scheme, with a tripartite agreement signed in September [1].** That is a 2026-11-01 announcement and nothing yet flies. **So when a proposal lands citing airport-led demand, check whether the route is operating and ask for actual arrival numbers; if the promoter cannot show them, treat the demand as unproven.** Our local sources [2][3] are only topic pages with no usable content, so I have no Puducherry occupancy, ARR or restaurant-sales data; collect from customer.

## What peers tell us
**Listed peers are growing strongly, but that is corporate and luxury India, not Puducherry mid-market.** ITC Hotels Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was Rs 1,054 crore, up 26 percent, with EBITDA up 37 percent [4]; Ventive reported 27 percent revenue growth and a 48 percent EBITDA margin in Q3 FY26 [5]; Leela's Q2 was driven by 30 percent RevPAR growth, entirely ARR-led [6]. **Read this as proof that room rates, not just occupancy, can move, and ask every borrower for their own ARR and occupancy trend.** The ICRA hotel methodology [8] and the CHL rational report [9] are undated and old; use them for structure logic only.

**Take every month: GST returns, bank statements of the collection account, OTA payout statements and a power bill.** Covenant on a minimum DSCR and on debt-funded capex above a stated limit; if the borrower proposes a second property before the first services debt, decline. **Avoid greenfield resorts, leased-asset rollouts and single-restaurant borrowers with no collateral.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the collection account, not the P&L.** Falling OTA payouts, rising cash withdrawals, power-bill arrears or staff-salary delays mean the daily cash engine has stalled. **If occupancy or covers drop for two consecutive months, ask for the booking register and re-rate the limit.**

Falling declared turnover against bank credits -> seek explanation and stop enhancement
Arrears or delayed salaries -> move to tighter monitoring and reduce exposure
Route still not operating -> do not credit airport-led demand in projections
Charge or encumbrance appears -> freeze fresh limits
